description:
A message copy never writes into a static literal's buffer.

deep_copy.rs:299 calls shared_bin_freeze (bits.rs:244) on every copied view. That includes the baked static SharedBin of a literal over 64 B, which is declared writable with room 0 (src/ir_codegen/aot_main.rs:217). Whichever scheduler thread sends does a non-atomic `room |= FROZEN` on shared program data. In practice the write is benign and idempotent; in the Rust memory model it is a data race.

The same arm makes one BinRef plus one atomic retain per copied view. That contradicts the documented rule of one BinRef per buffer per heap (runtime.md R15).

Fix:
- Static buffers read as frozen by construction: bake FROZEN into room at link time, or place them in rodata with the refcount handled as static.
- Freeze only a buffer that has room.
- Dedup BinRefs per gift if a measurement shows a message holding several views of one buffer.

Acceptance:
- A fixture sends a >64 B literal from several processes.
- The static buffer is read-only (rodata), or the code provably never stores to it.
- The BinRef count per gift is pinned.

Also here (from fz-9e2.2): SHARED_BIN_ROOM_OFFSET (runtime/src/bits.rs) is held only by a layout test while aot_main.rs hard-codes offsets 32..40. Baking the room word uses the constant, or the constant and its test go.
title: A message copy never writes into a static literal's buffer
